ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r7.claim: The apparent antecedent of the pronoun in “when he came to it” is the fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في جاءها عائد على النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r8.claim: Some identify its antecedent as the tree, described as green samur or ʿalayq which did not burn and receded whenever Moses approached.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r8.anchor: وقيل: على الشجرة، وكان قد رآها في شجرة سمر خضراء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r9.claim: The omitted subject of “he was called” is apparently Moses; the following an may be explanatory or a verbal noun construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r9.anchor: ونودي المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله، الظاهر أنه ضمير عائد على موسى عليه السلام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī denies that an is a lightened emphatic particle with an understood pronoun, because it would require qad, which cannot be deleted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r10.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: هل يجوز أن تكون المخففة من الثقيلة، وتقديره بأنه بورك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r11.claim: Abū Ḥayyān allows the lightened emphatic particle if bӯrika is a supplication, since qad is not used with a prayer; al-Zamakhsharī's objection assumes it is a report.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون المخففة من الثقيلة، وبورك فعل دعاء، كما تقول: بارك الله فيك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r12.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r12.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows an to form the passive's complement after dropping the preposition, as in “he was called with the license.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r12.anchor: وأجاز الزجاج أن تكون أن بورك في موضع المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r13.claim: Another analysis makes the omitted passive subject the calling itself, then explains it with the following words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r13.anchor: وقيل: المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله هو ضمير النداء، أي نودي هو، أي النداء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r14.claim: Bӯrika means being sanctified and purified, and having one's good increased; the phrase has several prepositional forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r14.anchor: وبورك معناه: قدس وطهر وزيد خيره، ويقال: باركك الله، وبارك فيك، وبارك عليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r1.claim: Three poetic examples illustrate the word bӯrika: an anonymous blessing of a newborn and elder, another image of the dead stranger, and a blessing by ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr for descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r1.anchor: فبوركت مولودا وبوركت ناشئا ... وبوركت عند الشيب إذ أنت أشيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, and others reportedly take “who is in the fire” to refer to God; Abū Ḥayyān says any sound report must be understood elliptically as God's power and authority there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس، وابن جبير، والحسن وغيرهم: أراد تعالى بمن في النار ذاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r3.speaker: قيل لموسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r3.claim: Another interpretation addresses Moses: blessed is whoever is in the place or direction where the fire appeared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r3.anchor: وقيل لموسى عليه السلام: أي بورك من في المكان أو الجهة التي لاح له فيها النار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r4.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r4.claim: Al-Suddī identifies those in the fire as the angels appointed over it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: من للملائكة الموكلين بها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r5.claim: Among interpretations treating “who” as non-rational, Ibn ʿAbbās identifies it as the light.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r6.claim: Another non-rational interpretation identifies it as the tree where the fire was burning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r6.anchor: وقيل: الشجرة التي تتقد فيها النار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r7.claim: The apparent reading takes “those around it” as rational beings, namely angels, supported by a transmitted explanatory reading that differs from the agreed written codex and is therefore not a canonical reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r7.anchor: والظاهر في ومن حولها أنه لمن يعلم تفسير يا موسى، وفسر بالملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r8.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r8.claim: A reading transmitted from Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿIkrima explains “those around it” as angels; Abū Ḥayyān treats it as commentary because it differs from the codex text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r8.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة أبي فيما نقل أبو عمرو الداني: وابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة ومن حولها من الملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r9.claim: Others interpret those around the fire as Moses together with the angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r9.anchor: وفسر أيضا بموسى والملائكة عليهم السلام معا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes the surrounding “who” as non-rational beings: the places around the fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r10.anchor: وقيل: تكون لما لا يعقل، وفسر بالأمكنة التي حول النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r11.claim: Blessing those present and around the fire suits the momentous event of God speaking to and commissioning Moses; beginning with blessing reassures and prepares him for the conversation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r11.anchor: وجدير أن يبارك من فيها ومن حواليها إذا حدث أمر عظيم، وهو تكليم الله لموسى عليه السلام وتنبيئه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r12.claim: The apparent reading includes the glorification under “he was called”; it declares God free of created attributes, especially if “who is in the fire” is taken to mean God and imply location.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r12.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: وسبحان الله رب العالمين داخل تحت قوله: نودي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r13.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r13.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses uttered the glorification on hearing the call to declare God transcendent beyond the attributes of created beings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r13.anchor: وقال السدي: هو من كلام موسى، لما سمع النداء قال: وسبحان الله رب العالمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r14.speaker: ابن شجرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r14.claim: Ibn Shajara says the words are God's: whoever glorifies God is blessed; Abū Ḥayyān finds this poorly supported by the wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r14.anchor: وقال ابن شجرة: هو من كلام الله، ومعناه: وبورك من سبح الله، وهذا بعيد من دلالة اللفظ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r15.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r15.claim: Another view addresses Muḥammad with the glorification as an interruption between the two speeches, intended to declare God's transcendence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p211/r15.anchor: وقيل: وسبحان الله رب العالمين خطاب لمحمد عليه الصلاة والسلام، وهو اعتراض بين الكلامين

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.claim: The account then recounts Moses encountering fire on the mountain, where God charged him to go to Pharaoh and free the Israelites.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.anchor: turns to Moses’ encounter with the fire on the mountain, from which God spoke charging him with his mission

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r8.claim: An is explanatory because a call contains the sense of speech; the meaning is that he was told, “Blessed is …”.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r8.anchor: هي المفسرة لأن النداء فيه معنى القول

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r9.claim: One reported interpretation takes “the one in the fire” as God, with fire meaning light and those around it meaning angels; Rāzī calls the Ibn ʿAbbās report fabricated.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r9.anchor: وهو مروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وإن كنا نقطع بأن هذه الرواية موضوعة مختلفة

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r10.speaker: قتادة والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r10.claim: Qatāda and al-Zajjāj take the one in the fire to be God’s light and those around it to be the angels.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r10.anchor: هو نور الله ، { ومن حولها } الملائكة ، وهو مروي عن قتادة والزجاج

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r11.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r11.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says God spoke to Moses through speech heard from the tree in the blessed spot; God created the speech in the tree, which was in the fire, while angels were around it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r11.anchor: أن الله تعالى ناداه بكلام سمعه من الشجرة في البقعة المباركة فكانت الشجرة محلا للكلام

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r12.claim: Rāzī finds the nearer view that Moses is the one in the fire because he was close to it, while those around it are angels; proximity can be described as being inside something.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r12.anchor: وهذا أقرب لأن القريب من الشيء قد يقال إنه فيه

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r13.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the phrase as referring to the place of the fire and the area around that place, the blessed spot mentioned in 28:30.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r13.anchor: أي من في مكان النار ومن حول مكانها هي البقعة التي حصلت فيها

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r14.speaker: أبي
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r14.claim: Ubayy’s readings include “Blessed is the earth and what is around it” and “Blessed is the fire.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r14.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة أبي ( تباركت الأرض ومن حولها ) وعنه أيضا ( بوركت النار )

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r1.claim: The spot and those around it were blessed because God spoke to Moses there, appointed him a messenger, and showed him miracles; Syria is blessed in 21:71 for this reason.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r1.anchor: حدوث هذا الأمر العظيم فيها وهو تكليم الله موسى عليه السلام وجعله رسولا

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r2.claim: Syria deserves blessing as the birthplace of prophets, the place where revelation descends, and their resting place in life and death.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r2.anchor: مبعث الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم ، ومهبط الوحي وكفاتهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r3.claim: The blessing announcement prepares for Moses’ private conversation by signaling that an immense event has occurred, whose blessing spreads through all Syria.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r3.anchor: يدل على أنه قد قضى أمر عظيم تنتشر البركة منه في أرض الشام كلها

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r4.claim: The glorification has two purposes: to deny what does not befit God’s essence or wisdom, preparing for the proof of Moses’ mission, and to announce that the Lord of the worlds wills and creates this great event.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r4.anchor: نزه نفسه عما لا يليق به في ذاته وحكمته ليكون ذلك مقدمة في صحة رسالة موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r8.claim: Sunnis offer two ways Moses could know the caller was God: he heard speech unlike letters or sounds and knew necessarily it was God’s attribute, or he heard a voice from the tree.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r8.anchor: أنه سمع الكلام المنزه عن مشابهة الحروف والأصوات فعلم بالضرورة

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r9.speaker: أئمة ما وراء النهر
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r9.claim: Transoxanian imams say Moses heard a voice from the tree, then ask what established that the caller was God.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r9.anchor: قول أئمة ما وراء النهر وهو أنه عليه السلام سمع الصوت من الشجرة

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r10.speaker: أئمة ما وراء النهر
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r10.claim: Their first proof—that a human cannot make a call from fire or a tree—is weak, since Satan could enter the fire or tree and call.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r10.anchor: لأن أحدا منا لا يقدر عليه وهو ضعف لاحتمال أن يقال الشيطان دخل في النار والشجرة

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r11.speaker: أئمة ما وراء النهر
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r11.claim: Their second proof, that the voice’s magnitude must be miraculous, is weak because the powers of angels and devils are unknown and could account for any magnitude.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r11.anchor: وهو أيضا ضعيف لأنا لا نعرف مقادير قوى الملائكة والشياطين فلا قدر إلا ويجوز صدوره منهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r12.claim: The soundest proof is an accompanying miracle: the fire burned in a green tree without consuming it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p156/r12.anchor: إن النار كانت مشتعلة في شجرة خضراء لم تحترق

BURSEVI:v6p234/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r1.claim: Moses came near a luminous fire that appeared without burning, seen from a tree identified as a samrah.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r1.anchor: (س آن هنكام كه آمد موسى نزديك آن آتش نوراني ديد بي إحراق از درختي بسزد

BURSEVI:v6p234/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r2.claim: The call was audible speech reaching Moses from the direction of the mountain.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r2.anchor: جاءه النداء وهو الكلام المسموع من جانب الطور.

BURSEVI:v6p234/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r3.speaker: عرائس البيان
BURSEVI:v6p234/r3.claim: Moses was initially in the station of love and ambiguous unveiling; God made the tree and fire a mirror for manifestation of majesty and beauty, keeping Moses within human capacity to approach rather than perish in the first overwhelming disclosure.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r3.anchor: قال في "عرائس البيان" : كان موسى عليه السلام في بداية حاله في مقام العشق والمحبة

BURSEVI:v6p234/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r4.claim: An either explains the content of the call or is a source particle with its preposition omitted according to a regular construction.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r4.anchor: {أن} مفسرة لما في النداء من معنى القول ، أي : {بورك} أو بأن بورك على أنها مصدرية حذف منها الجار

BURSEVI:v6p234/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r5.claim: Būrika is passive from bāraka, ‘was made blessed’; ‘whoever is in the fire’ is its deputy subject.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r5.anchor: وبورك مجهول بارك وهوخبر لادعاء أي جعل مباركا وهو ما فيه الخير والبركة والقائم مقام الفاعل قوله : {من فى النار}

BURSEVI:v6p234/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r6.claim: The phrase refers to whoever is in the place of the fire, the blessed plot also named in the account of Moses’ call in 28:30.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r6.anchor: أي من في مكان النار وهو البقعة المباركة المذكورة في قوله تعالى : {نودي من شاطىا الواد الايمن فى البقعة المباركة}

BURSEVI:v6p234/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r7.claim: Those around it include the blessed land of Syria, abode and burial place of prophets, especially the spot where God spoke to Moses.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r7.anchor: أي ومن حول مكانها والظاهر أن المبارك فيه عام في كل من في تلك البقعة وحواليها من أرض الشام

BURSEVI:v6p234/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r8.claim: The opening blessing announces Moses’ great religious destiny: divine speech, prophethood, miracles, and blessings spreading through the Holy Land.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r8.anchor: وفي ابتداء خطاب الله موسى بذلك عند مجيئه بشارة بأنه قد قضى له أمر عظيم ديني تنتشر بركاته في أقطار الأرض المقدسة

BURSEVI:v6p234/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r9.claim: A place where God is witnessed and speaks becomes blessed; a poet illustrates this by saying Salmā’s valley becomes fresh and fertile when she arrives.

BURSEVI:v6p234/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234/r10.claim: The spiritual states of God’s men make even their footprints in deserts and mountains bring greenness through blessing from God.
BURSEVI:v6p234/r10.anchor: ولم يزل يخضر مواطىء أقدام رجال الله في الصحاري والجبال من بركات حالاتهم مع الله

BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r1.claim: Some commentators understand the blessing as a greeting; al-Kashifi glosses it ‘may [he] be blessed.’
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r1.anchor: ثم إن بعض المفسرين حمل بورك على التحية كما قال الكاشفي : )بركت داده باد (

BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r2.claim: Some interpret ‘whoever is in the fire’ as the angels, blessed along with the light that appeared.
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r2.anchor: وبعضهم حمل من في النار على الملائكة وذلك أن النور الذي بان قد بارك فيه وفي الملائكة

BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r3.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r3.claim: Some gnostics take the phrase to mean God, who grants Moses the blessing of witnessing Him; He may manifest through fire, light, tree, or mountain while remaining beyond direction.
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : إن الله أراد بمن في النار ذاته المقدسة وهو الذي أفاض بركة مشاهدته على موسى

BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r4.claim: Manifestation through fire, light, tree, or mountain does not place God or His attributes in a direction.
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r4.anchor: وله تعالى أن يتجلى بوصف النار والنور والشجرة والطور وغيرها مما يليق بحال العاشق مع تنزه ذاته وصفاته عن الجهة في الحقيقة

BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r5.claim: The source invokes a hadith stating that God is seen in whatever form of His essence He wills.
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن الله يرى هيئة ذاته كيف يشاء"

BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r6.claim: The doxology completes the call, guarding against imagining likeness from hearing God’s speech and expressing wonder at the event’s greatness.
BURSEVI:v6p234#2/r6.anchor: من تمام ما نودي به لئلا يتوهم من سماع كلامه تشبيها وللتعجيب من عظمة ذلك الأمر.

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r1.claim: The One in the fire is understood to refer to God Himself.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r1.anchor: The One in the fire is understood to refer to God Himself

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r2.claim: One interpretation is that the fire itself is blessed.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r2.anchor: according to some, this phrase means that it was the fire that was blessed

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that the Light of God within the fire is blessed.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r3.anchor: or that the Light of God within the fire was blessed

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r4.claim: The one around the fire may refer to the angels, who are blessed by God.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r4.anchor: The one around it refers to the angels

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r5.claim: Alternatively, the one around the fire may be Moses together with the angels, blessed by God.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r5.anchor: or to Moses and the angels together (Ṭ), meaning that Moses and the angels are blessed by God

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r6.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r6.claim: Although man ordinarily means who or one who, it can have the broader sense of mā, meaning what.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r6.anchor: the Arabic particle man, which is rendered here as the one, but ordinarily means

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r7.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r7.claim: On that broader reading, the phrase means that what is in the fire—the fire itself—is blessed.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r7.anchor: it would mean, “Blessed is that which is in the fire,”

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r8.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r8.claim: In light of 28:30’s description of the site as blessed, some take blessed to mean the place of the fire, site of the great event.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r8.anchor: some interpret blessed to mean that it is the place of the fire that is blessed

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r9.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r9.claim: Another gloss is blessed is the one seeking after the fire.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r9.anchor: Blessed is the one [seeking after] the fire

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r10.speaker: still others
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r10.claim: Another gloss is blessed is the One whose power and authority is in the fire.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r10.anchor: Blessed is the One [whose power and authority is] in the fire

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r11.claim: The various glosses arise partly because bāraka ordinarily takes a direct or indirect object, but this clause supplies none.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r11.anchor: ordinarily this form of the verb

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r12.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r12.claim: The passive būrika can also mean holy, or muqaddas.

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r13.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r13.claim: Though called fire, the phenomenon was actually light; Arabs sometimes used nār in place of nūr, and Moses called it fire.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r13.anchor: Some note that the phenomenon was described as fire

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās said it was not fire but flickering light, and elsewhere called it the Light of the Lord of the worlds; no grading is stated.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r14.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās said it was not fire, but a flickering light

STUDYQURAN:27:8/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r15.speaker: a ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r15.claim: A hadith says God does not sleep, raises the deeds of night and day, and has a veil of light or fire; if removed, the glory of His Face would burn everything seen. No grading is given.
STUDYQURAN:27:8/r15.anchor: God sleeps not; nor is it proper to Him to sleep. He lowers justice and raises it. He raises to Himself the deeds of the night before the day

TAB-FULL:v18p10/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r1.claim: Moses came to the fire he had seen from afar; the fire was the warmth stop for his party against the cold.
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فلما جاءها} [النمل: 8] يقول: فلما جاء موسى النار التي آنسها {نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها} [النمل: 8] .

TAB-FULL:v18p10/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the blessing as sanctification.
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {نودي أن بورك من في النار} [النمل: 8] يقول: قدس

TAB-FULL:v18p10/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r3.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r3.claim: Some exegetes take the one in the fire to be God Himself and say the fire was His light.
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: عنى جل جلاله بذلك نفسه، وهو الذي كان في النار، وكانت النار نوره تعالى ذكره في قول جماعة من أهل التأويل.

TAB-FULL:v18p10/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the phrase means God Himself, whose light was in the tree.
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك من في النار} [النمل: 8] يعني نفسه؛ قال: كان نور رب العالمين في الشجرة

TAB-FULL:v18p10/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Moses was called while he was in the fire.
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قول الله: " {بورك من في النار} [النمل: 8] قال: ناداه وهو في النار

TAB-FULL:v18p10/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r6.claim: Al-Hasan identifies what was in the fire as light.
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: " {نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها} [النمل: 8] قال: هو النور

TAB-FULL:v18p10/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r7.claim: Qatādah says that God's light was blessed.
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r7.anchor: قال معمر: قال قتادة: " {بورك من في النار} [النمل: 8] قال: نور الله بورك

TAB-FULL:v18p10/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r8.speaker: مجاهد، ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r8.claim: Mujāhid says the fire itself was blessed, and the segment notes that Ibn ʿAbbās held the same view.
TAB-FULL:v18p10/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {نودي أن بورك، من في النار} [النمل: 8] بوركت النار " كذلك قاله ابن عباس

TAB-FULL:v18p12/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r1.claim: Mujāhid again explains the blessing as being upon the fire itself.
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: " {بورك من في النار} [النمل: 8] قال: بوركت النار

TAB-FULL:v18p12/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r2.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says it is the light of the Merciful, identifies light with God, and reads the following praise as glorification of God, Lord of the worlds.
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب، في قوله: " {أن بورك من في النار} [النمل: 8] نور الرحمن، والنور هو الله {وسبحان الله رب العالمين} [النمل: 8]

TAB-FULL:v18p12/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r3.speaker: أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r3.claim: Exegetes differ whether fire here means light or the actual fire; the latter reading is supported by Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's report about the veils.
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r3.anchor: معناه: النور كما ذكرت عمن ذكرت ذلك عنه. وقال آخرون: معناه النار لا النور.

TAB-FULL:v18p12/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr lists veils of might, dominion, authority, fire, light, cloud, and water, and identifies this as the fire from which Moses was called.
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، أنه قال: " حجاب العزة، وحجاب الملك، وحجاب السلطان، وحجاب النار، وهي تلك النار التي نودي منها.

TAB-FULL:v18p12/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r5.claim: Saʿīd explains the wording without a second preposition by the Arabic idiom bārakaka Allāh, though Arabs also say bāraka fīka Allāh.
TAB-FULL:v18p12/r5.anchor: وإنما قيل: بورك من في النار، ولم يقل: بورك فيمن في النار على لغة الذين يقولون: باركك الله. والعرب تقول: باركك الله، وبارك فيك

TAB-FULL:v18p13/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p13/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p13/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Hasan identify those around the fire as angels.
TAB-FULL:v18p13/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {ومن حولها} [النمل: 8] قال: يعني الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v18p13/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p13/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v18p13/r2.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says those around it are Moses and the angels; the next verse then addresses Moses by name.
TAB-FULL:v18p13/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب، " {ومن حولها} [الأنعام: 92] قال: موسى النبي والملائكة، ثم قال: {يا موسى إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم} [النمل: 9]

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r1.claim: The five stories exemplify the sūra's opening promise and warning: promise predominates in the first three accounts of Moses, David, and Solomon, while warning predominates in the last two.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r1.anchor: بيان أول القصص الخمس التي أشير إليها في السورة استشهادا لما في صدرها من التبشير والإنذار

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r9.claim: To bless means to confer abundant good, as shown by Arabic expressions for blessing someone or placing blessing upon or in them.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r9.anchor: والمراد بالمباركة إعطاء الخير الكثير يقال باركه وبارك عليه وبارك فيه أي ألبسه الخير الكثير

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r1.claim: The parallel account in Ṭā Hā suggests Moses was among those around the fire, and that God's blessing consisted in choosing him after purifying him.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r1.anchor: ويستأنس منه أن المراد بمن حول النار موسى أو هو ممن حول النار، ومباركته اختياره بعد تقديسه

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r2.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r2.claim: One reported view takes the one in the fire as the manifestation of God's power there: God spoke from the tree surrounded by fire, blessed Moses, and was not physically located in space.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r2.anchor: قيل إن معناه من ظهر سلطانه وقدرته في النار فإن التكليم كان من الشجرة

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads the glorification as declaring God transcendent beyond embodiment, spatial enclosure, or temporal contiguity, rather than as Moses's exclamation of wonder.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r3.anchor: تنزيها له سبحانه من أن يكون جسما أو جسمانيا يحيط به المكان أو يجاوره الحدثان

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r4.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r4.claim: Another reported view identifies those in the fire as angels and the one around it as Moses.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد بمن في النار الملائكة الحاضرون فيها كما أن المراد بمن حولها موسى

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r5.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r5.claim: A further view reverses those identifications: Moses is in the fire and angels are around it.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد به موسى عليه السلام وبمن حولها الملائكة

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r6.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r6.claim: An elliptical reading supplies “the place containing the fire”: Moses is in the blessed site, while the surrounding holy land is Syria, inhabited by prophets descended from Abraham and Israel.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r6.anchor: وقيل في الكلام تقدير والأصل بورك من في المكان الذي فيه النار - وهو البقعة المباركة التي

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r7.speaker: قول غير مسمى
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r7.claim: Other reported readings take the one in the fire to be God's light, or the tree itself; Moses or the praising angels are respectively around it.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد بمن في النار نور الله تعالى وبمن حولها موسى. وقيل المراد بمن في النار الشجرة فإنها كانت محاطة بالنار بمن حولها الملائكة المسبحون

TABATABAI:27:8-10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī judges most of these proposed identifications to be visibly forced.
TABATABAI:27:8-10/r8.anchor: وأكثر هذه الوجوه لا يخلو من تحكم ظاهر

TABRISI:27:3-8/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:3-8/r20.claim: Moses reached what he thought was a fire, though it was light.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r20.anchor: أي جاء موسى إلى النار يعني التي ظن أنها نار وهي نور

TABRISI:27:3-8/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r21.speaker: وهب
TABRISI:27:3-8/r21.claim: Wahb describes fire issuing from a branch of a vivid green tree; it grew hotter without burning it while the tree grew greener, and Moses approached then retreated before the call.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r21.anchor: قال وهب: لما رأى موسى النار وقف قريبا منها فرآها تخرج من فرع شجرة خضراء

TABRISI:27:3-8/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:3-8/r22.claim: The call is revelation: those in the fire are angels and the one around it is Moses; the light held angels praising God, and the blessing's prayer form intends a report.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r22.anchor: والمراد به نداء الوحي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها أي بورك فيمن في النار

TABRISI:27:8-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r1.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:27:8-10/r1.claim: Al-Kisai says Arabic usage permits barakahu Allah, baraka alayhi, and baraka fihi.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r1.anchor: قال الكسائي: تقول العرب باركه الله وبارك عليه وبارك فيه.

TABRISI:27:8-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:27:8-10/r2.claim: This view takes the one in the fire as God's authority, power, and proof, so blessing refers to God as source of the light; those around it are Moses and the angels.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير.

TABRISI:27:8-10/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r3.claim: Another view supplies an omitted noun: blessed is the seeker of the fire, Moses, and those around it are the angels; the blessing remains on Moses and the angels.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه بورك من طلب النار وهو موسى ع فحذف المضاف ومن حولها الملائكة

TABRISI:27:8-10/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r4.claim: God's greeting of Moses with blessing is compared with the angels' greeting of Abraham's household with mercy and blessings.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r4.anchor: حين دخلوا عليه فقالوا رحمة الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت.

TABRISI:27:8-10/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:8-10/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:8-10/r5.claim: Glorifying God declares Him beyond being a body needing direction, an accident needing a substrate, or one who speaks with an instrument.
TABRISI:27:8-10/r5.anchor: تنزيها له عما لا يليق بصفاته تعالى عن أن يكون جسما يحتاج إلى جهة أو عرضا يحتاج إلى محل

THALABI:v7p189#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v7p189#2/r1.claim: The Prophet said God neither sleeps nor should sleep, raises and lowers the scales, receives night deeds before day deeds and day deeds before night deeds, and is veiled by fire that would burn all it sees if unveiled.
THALABI:v7p189#2/r1.anchor: قام بيننا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأربع فقال: «إن الله عز وجل لا ينام،

THALABI:v7p189#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v7p189#2/r2.claim: After the prophetic report, Abu Ubayda recited the verse about blessing in the fire and those around it.
THALABI:v7p189#2/r2.anchor: ثم قرأ أبو عبيدة أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها

THALABI:v7p189#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r3.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p189#2/r3.claim: One explanation takes the blessed one in the fire to mean God's authority and power, and those around it.
THALABI:v7p189#2/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه: بورك من في النار سلطانه وقدرته وفيمن حولها.

THALABI:v7p189#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v7p189#2/r4.claim: Others say the blessing concerns Moses and the angels; being in the fire means seeking or approaching it, as ordinary Arabic can name a destination before one reaches its center.

THALABI:v7p189#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p189#2/r5.claim: The verse blesses Moses and the angels around the fire; God thereby greets and honors Moses, as angels greeted Abraham's household.
THALABI:v7p189#2/r5.anchor: وهذا تحية من الله سبحانه لموسى وتكرمة له كما حيا إبراهيم على ألسنة الملائكة

THALABI:v7p189#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v7p189#2/r6.claim: Some identify the fire itself as the recipient of the blessing.
THALABI:v7p189#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذه البركة راجعة إلى النار نفسها.

THALABI:v7p189#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p189#2/r7.claim: Mujahid transmitted Ibn Abbas's explanation that the fire was blessed; Ibn Abbas also reported hearing Ubayy recite “Blessed be the fire and whoever is around it.”
THALABI:v7p189#2/r7.anchor: روى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس أنه قال: معناه بوركت النار،

THALABI:v7p189#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r8.speaker: أبي
THALABI:v7p189#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says he heard Ubayy recite “بوركت النار ومن حولها,” supporting the interpretation that the fire itself is blessed.
THALABI:v7p189#2/r8.anchor: سمعت أبيا يقرؤها: أن بوركت النار ومن حولها،

THALABI:v7p189#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p189#2/r9.claim: For the fire-centered interpretation, min can mean ma, and ma can be an extra particle; the resulting sense is blessing upon the fire and those around it, Moses and the angels.
THALABI:v7p189#2/r9.anchor: قد تكون صلة في كثير من المواضع كقوله جند ما هنالك

THALABI:v7p189#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p189#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p189#2/r10.claim: The fire is called blessed by analogy with the Qur'an's description of the blessed spot.
THALABI:v7p189#2/r10.anchor: فسمى النار مباركة كما سمى البقعة مباركة

THALABI:v7p190/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p190/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p190/r1.claim: Arabic uses four constructions for blessing: barakaka Allah, baraka fīk, baraka ʿalayk, and baraka lak; an anonymous poem illustrates the forms.
THALABI:v7p190/r1.anchor: فإن العرب تقول: باركك الله، وبارك فيك، وبارك عليك وبارك لك، أربع لغات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r1.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r1.claim: Al-Farra’ says أن is accusative if Moses is implicit as the subject of the passive verb, but nominative if he is not; al-Zajjaj gives the same analysis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r1.anchor: قال الفراء (أن) في موضع نصب إذا أضمرت اسم موسى في (نودي) وإن لم تضمر اسم موسى كانت (أن) في موضع رفع. ونحو هذا قال الزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r2.claim: Al-Farra’ notes Arabic uses baraka with God as object and with عليه or فيه; a cited poem exemplifies the passive blessing formula.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: العرب تقول: باركه الله، وبارك عليه، وبارك فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi prefers an ellipsis meaning “blessed is the one seeking the fire,” namely Moses; it is God’s greeting to him, like the blessing spoken to Abraham’s household.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r3.anchor: فالأحسن: أن الآية من باب حذف المضاف على تقدير: بورك من في طلب النار، وهو موسى عليه السلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r4.claim: Abu Ali takes the phrase as someone near the fire, not someone plunged into it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: {بورك من في النار} من في قرب النار ليس يراد به: متوغلها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r5.claim: They interpret “the one in the fire” as God, saying He is sanctified there; the author notes that attributing blessing to God is like saying God is blessed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة في قوله: {بورك من في النار}: قدس من في النار، وهو الله سبحانه؛ عني به نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r6.claim: The fire here is light that Moses mistook for fire; God appeared to him through its signs and speech, so the verse means God was blessed in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r6.anchor: والمراد بالنار هاهنا: النور، وذلك أن موسى رأى نورا عظيما فظنه نارا لذلك ذكرها هنا بلفظ النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r7.claim: A Torah wording, “God came from Sinai,” means God sent Moses from Sinai; similarly, God was described as in the fire because He became known to Moses through it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r7.anchor: وهذا كما روي أنه مكتوب في التوراة: جاء الله من سيناء يعني: بعث الله موسى من سيناء حتى يدعو الخلق إليه، ويعرفهم توحيده ودينه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r8.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r8.claim: Some interpret the one in the fire as God’s power and authority, omitted because it is understood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p164/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: على هذا القول تقدير الآية: {من في النار} سلطانه وقدرته، فحذف للإحاطة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r1.speaker: مجاهد وأبيّ
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r1.claim: Mujahid says the blessing is upon the fire itself, which fits Ubayy’s reading “that the fire be blessed”; al-Wahidi says this does not fit the standard reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r1.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد في هذه الآية أنه قال: معناه: وبوركت النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r2.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says angels were in the fire, so “those in the fire” refers to angels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: كان في النار ملائكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r3.speaker: جماعة من أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r3.claim: A group of exegetes identify the one in the fire as God’s light; here من means “what,” and God created light in the fire Moses saw.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r3.anchor: وروي أيضا عن جماعة من أهل التفسير أنهم قالوا: {من في النار} نور الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r4.claim: Everyone takes those around the fire as the angels and Moses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ومن حولها} هم الملائكة وموسى، في قول الجميع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r5.claim: Angels stood around the light Moses saw, loudly glorifying and sanctifying God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r5.anchor: وذلك أنه كان حول ذلك النور الذي رأى موسى ملائكة، لهم زجل بالتسبيح والتقديس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r6.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r6.claim: Abu Ali means those near but not so close as someone entering the fire; Moses is the one taking from it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p167/r6.anchor: وقال أبو علي: {ومن حولها} ومن لم يقرب منها قرب الآخذ فيها وهو موسى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p169/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p169/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p169/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that “Glory be to God” means God declares Himself transcendent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p169/r1.anchor: وسبحان الله رب العالمين} قال ابن عباس: نزه نفسه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r9.claim: The words refer to the one seeking and approaching the fire; the meaning is, “Blessed are you, Moses.”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r9.anchor: أي: من في طلب النار وقصدها، والمعنى: بورك فيك يا موسى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r10.claim: Those around the fire are the angels.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r11.claim: This is God’s greeting to Moses and an honor bestowed on him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r11.anchor: وهذا تحية من الله سبحانه لموسى وتكرمة له

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r12.claim: The phrase declares God free of every defect.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r4.claim: Moses came to the fire he saw before himself.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r4.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {فلما جاءها} [النمل: 8] جاء إلى النار عند نفسه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r5.claim: In Qatāda’s explanation as transmitted by Saʿīd, Moses was what appeared to be in the fire: it was the light of the Lord of the worlds.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r5.anchor: يعني بقوله: {بورك من في النار} [النمل: 8] نفسه، وإنما كان ضوء نور رب العالمين، في تفسير سعيد عن قتادة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r6.claim: Qatāda identifies those around the fire as angels.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r7.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s codex reads, “Blessed is the fire and whoever is around it.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r7.anchor: وهي في مصحف أبي بن كعب: نودي أن بوركت النار ومن حولها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r8.claim: The passage glorifies God, Lord of the worlds.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r8.anchor: {وسبحان الله رب العالمين {8} يا موسى إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم {9} وألق عصاك} [النمل: 8-10] فألقاها.

QASHANI:27:8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:8/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:8/r1.claim: The blessed one in the fire is the heart of Moses, which reaches the fire through manifestations of divine attributes, finding real perfections and the prophetic station of intimate speech.
QASHANI:27:8/r1.anchor: هو موسى القلب الواصل إلى النار بتجليات الصفات الإلهية ووجدان الكمالات الحقيقية ومقام المكالمة عن النبوة

QASHANI:27:8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:8/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:8/r2.claim: Those around the fire are spiritual faculties and celestial angels, receiving illuminations of unveiling, secret knowledge and wisdom, sacred confirmations, and inward states of spiritual tasting.
QASHANI:27:8/r2.anchor: من القوى الروحانية والملائكة السماوية بأنوار المكاشفة وأسرار العلوم والحكم والتأييدات القدسية والأحوال السرية والذوقية

QASHANI:27:8/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:8/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:8/r3.claim: Glorifying God means transcending the divine essence by shedding psychic qualities, bodily veils, defects, and faults.
QASHANI:27:8/r3.anchor: ونزه ذات الله بتجردك عن الصفات النفسانية والغواشي الجسدانية والنقائص والمعائب

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r6.claim: The location is the blessed spot by the right side of the valley and the tree, as described in al-Qaṣaṣ 28:30; a prophetic station is sacred, so those there and around the fire receive blessing, including Moses.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r6.anchor: mübarek bir buk‘adır. Enbiyâ makamı bir mukaddes yerdir. Bu buk‘ada bulunan ve bu ateşin etrafında dolaşan kimseler berekâta mazhar olmuştur.

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r7.speaker: Kâdî Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r7.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī and exegetes like him take the phrase broadly: the blessed people near the fire include Moses as one member of the group.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r7.anchor: Kâdî Beyzâvî gibi müfessirînin kabul ettikleri bu tefsire göre bu ateşi hisseden yalnız Mûsâ değildir.

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r8.claim: Some exegetes instead say that the one in the fire is Moses, since he was the one who came to it.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r8.anchor: Fakat bazı müfessirîn bu ateşe gelen Mûsâ olmakla مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ Mûsâ’dır demişler

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r9.claim: The appended declaration of divine transcendence conveys wonder at the event’s greatness and prevents any thought of likening God to creation.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r9.anchor: bu tesbih ve tenzih, vâkı‘anın azametine taaccüb ettirmekle beraber teşbih tevehhümüne meydan bırakmamak içindir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r2.claim: Commentators say the light Moses took for fire was actually divine light.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r2.anchor: Müfessirler, Hz. Mûsâ’nın ateş sandığı ışığın gerçekte ilâhî bir nur olduğunu belirtirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur identifies the one blessed at the fire as Moses and those around it as Gabriel and the angels assigned to illuminate the place.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r3.anchor: bulunduğu yerde mübarek kılınandan maksat Hz. Mûsâ, çevresindekiler ise Cebrâil ve o yeri aydınlatmakla görevli meleklerdir (İbn Âşûr, XIX, 226).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r4.speaker: Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r4.claim: Asad reads the fire metaphorically as the spiritual illumination specific to prophets, with Moses in it and his believers around him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r4.anchor: Mecazi anlamda ateş peygamberlere mahsus mânevî aydınlanma olarak da yorumlanmıştır (Esed, II, 763).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r5.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r5.claim: Zamakhshari takes the fire to mean Moses’s location; those blessed are Moses and the sacred lands around that place.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r5.anchor: Zemahşerî’ye göre ateşten maksat onun bulunduğu yerdir. Burada mübarek kılınanlar ise Mûsâ ile o yerin çevresinde bulunan kutsal topraklardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r6.claim: The verse stresses that God is Lord of all humanity, not only Israel, and the next verse calls Him absolutely victorious and wise, warranting reliance on Him in the struggle for monotheism.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r6.anchor: sadece İsrâiloğulları’nın değil, âlemlerin, bütün insanlığın rabbi olduğu vurgulanmakta, 9. âyette ise Allah’ın mutlak galip ve hikmet sahibi olduğu belirtilerek tevhid mücadelesinde ancak O’na güvenip dayanmak gerektiğine işaret edilmektedir

BAQILLANI:v1p189/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r2.claim: The call of blessing and glorification flows into the following account of divine lordship and the signs of Moses’ staff and hand, with no break in the composition.
BAQILLANI:v1p189/r2.anchor: فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها وسبحان الله رب العالمين

BURHAN:v1p130/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r9.claim: Ṭā Hā says فلما أتاها, while al-Naml says فلما جاءها.
BURHAN:v1p130/r9.anchor: فى طه ﴿ فلما أتاها ﴾ وفى النمل ﴿ فلما جاءها ﴾

BURHAN:v3p350/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p350/r1.speaker: النحاة
BURHAN:v3p350/r1.claim: Grammarians take an after the blessing as explanatory because explanatory an follows a verb with the meaning of saying, as in 'I wrote to him: return.'
BURHAN:v3p350/r1.anchor: إن أن هذه مفسرة لا تأتي إلا بعد فعل في معنى القول

SULAMI:v2p85#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p85#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p85#4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says Moses saw fire outwardly, but its reality was lights: God removed attachment to the fire, drew him into intimacy with its Illuminator, addressed him, restrained his speech, and singled him out among the messengers.
SULAMI:v2p85#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اصابتك بركة النار بموارد الأنوار عليك ومخاطبة الحق إياك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p31#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p31#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p31#4/r1.claim: The Messenger’s tazkiya is his taking the alms; the cited wording is “he purifies you.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p31#4/r1.anchor: و (التزكية) من الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله، أخذ الزكاة. قال: {يتلو عليكم آياتنا ويزكيكم} (3)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p31#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p31#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p31#4/r2.claim: The root sense of zakāh is growth and increase; alms are named zakāh because they make wealth grow, as crops grow and spending is blessed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p31#4/r2.anchor:
وأصل الزكاة النماء والزيادة. ومنه قيل للصدقة عن المال: زكاة لأنها
تثمره، ومنه يقال: زكا الزرع، وزكت النفقة: إذا بورك فيها.

NAHHAS:v3p197/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r14.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p197/r14.claim: Abu Ishaq parses أن as accusative, meaning because; it may alternatively be nominative as the passive subject.
NAHHAS:v3p197/r14.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق أن في موضع نصب أي بأنه قال ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع

NAHHAS:v3p197/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r15.speaker: أبي وابن عباس ومجاهد
NAHHAS:v3p197/r15.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy, Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid says بوركت النار ومن حولها; Abu Hatim's report has no sound chain and, if valid, is explanatory only.
NAHHAS:v3p197/r15.anchor: وحكى أبو حاتم أن في قراءة أبي وابن عباس ومجاهد ( أن بوركت النار ومن حولها )

NAHHAS:v3p197/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r16.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v3p197/r16.claim: Qatada identifies those in the fire and around it as angels.
NAHHAS:v3p197/r16.anchor: وقد روى سعيد عن قتادة أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها قال الملائكة

NAHHAS:v3p197/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r17.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p197/r17.claim: Al-Kisa'i cites the Arab expressions باركك الله and بارك فيك.
NAHHAS:v3p197/r17.anchor: وحكى الكسائي عن العرب باركك الله وبارك فيك

SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r1.claim: If the passive subject of nūdiya is Mūsā, an may be explanatory, masdariyya with an omitted preposition, or lightened from anna with an implicit pronoun of شأن; as a prayer, bӯrika needs no separator.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r1.anchor: وهو الظاهر. وفي " أن " حينئذ ثلاثة أوجه

SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects lightened anna because he requires qad before the predicate and says it cannot be omitted as a particle; that assumes bӯrika is declarative, not a prayer.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: هل يجوز أن تكون المخففة من الثقيلة، والتقدير: بأنه بورك. والضمير ضمير الشأن والقصة؟ قلت: لا لأنه لا بد من

SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r3.claim: If bӯrika is a prayer as in the earlier discussion of 24:9, no separator is needed, though the author notes the difficulty that a request normally cannot be the predicate of lightened anna.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r3.anchor: أما إذا قلنا: إنه دعاء كما تقدم في النور

SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r4.claim: Alternatively, the whole phrase an bӯrika can be the passive subject, with a deleted preposition; an may be masdariyya or lightened.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r4.anchor: أن القائم مقام الفاعل نفس " أن بورك " على حذف حرف الجر

SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r5.claim: A third analysis makes the passive subject an implicit verbal noun: “the call was called,” then explained by what follows, as in the story of Joseph.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8/r5.anchor: أنه ضمير المصدر المفهوم من الفعل أي: نودي النداء، ثم فسر بما بعده

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r1.claim: Man fī al-nār is the passive subject of bӯrika; bāraka can take a direct object and occurs in several prepositional constructions, as the cited poems attest.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r1.anchor: " من " قائم مقام الفاعل ل " بورك ". وبارك يتعدى بنفسه

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r2.claim: An unnamed poet attests bāraka with a direct object, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr attests it with fī.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r2.anchor: فبوركت مولودا وبوركت ناشئا وبوركت عند الشيب

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr’s poem witnesses the construction bӯrika fī.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r3.anchor:
وقال عبد الله بن الزبير:
3540 فبورك في بنيك وفي بنيهم

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r4.claim: A further anonymous poem attests the same blessing verb with fī.

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r5.claim: One view takes “those in the fire” as God, with an omitted muḍāf meaning His power and dominion in the fire.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r5.anchor: والمراد ب " من ": إما الباري تعالى، وهو على حذف مضاف

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r6.claim: Another view identifies those in and around the fire as Mūsā and the angels.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: المراد به موسى والملائكة، وكذلك بمن حولها

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r7.claim: A further view takes man as nonrational things: the light and the surrounding places.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: المراد ب " من " غير العقلاء وهو النور والأمكنة

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r8.claim: Subḥāna Allāh may continue the call, making both blessing and glorification the content of the summons.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r8.anchor: أنه من تتمة النداء أي: نودي بالبركة وتنزيه رب العزة

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r9.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r9.claim: Another analysis treats it as God’s address to Muḥammad, an interruption within the narrative.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r9.anchor: أنه من كلام الله تعالى مخاطبا لنبينا محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r10.claim: A third interpretation expands the phrase as “blessed is whoever glorifies God,” omitting man and its relative clause; subḥān is governed by an omitted cognate verb, not qāla.
SAMIN-DURR:27:8#2/r10.anchor: يعني أنه حذف " من " وصلتها وأبقى معمول الصلة

ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r6.claim: أن may be accusative with an implicit passive subject in نودي, or nominative as the passive subject itself.
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r6.anchor: إن شئت كان نصبا وإن شئت كان رفعا

ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r7.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r7.claim: The exegetical explanation identifies the one in the fire as God's light.
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r7.anchor: أن (من في النار) ههنا نور الله

ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r8.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r8.claim: Those around the fire are identified as angels or as God's light.

ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r9.claim: سبحان الله means declaring God exalted above evil; this is attributed to the Prophet and language scholars.
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r9.anchor: معناه تنزيه الله تبارك وتعالى عن السوء

ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r1.claim: Zamakhshari explains hawlaha as meaning "around it."
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r1.anchor: Thus Zamakhshari explains the expression hawlaha (lit., "around it").

ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r2.speaker: some of the earliest commentators, quoted by Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r2.claim: Early commentators read the fire as the light God bestows on prophets; Asad supposes their spiritual sensitivity makes them inherently near it.
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r2.anchor: According to some of the earliest commentators, quoted by Tabari, the "fire" (nar) is in this context synonymous with "light" (nur),

ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase may refer to God's own light, which encompasses and is the core of all spiritual illumination.
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n7/r3.anchor: Alternatively, the phrase man fi 'n-nar wa-man hawlaha may be 'inderstood as referring to God's Own light, which encompasses, and is the core of, all spiritual illumination.

ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n8/r1.claim: Asad points to 20:17–20 for comparison with this account of Moses.

ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n9/r1.claim: Asad points to note 14 on 20:20–21 for a tentative explanation of the symbolism of the staff miracle.
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n9/r1.anchor: For a tentative explanation of the symbolism underlying the miracle of the staff, see note 14 on 20:2O~2l.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p90/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p90/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p90/r1.claim: The author undertakes a comparison of the parallel Musa narratives because their broad similarity leaves meaningful wording differences to explain, including jāʾahā versus atāhā and adkhil versus usluk.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p90/r1.anchor: بينهما تشابهاً كبيراً ولا يتبيّن سِرُّ الاختلاف في التعبير بينهما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r5.claim: The parallel accounts differ between jāʾahā in Naml and atāhā in al-Qaṣaṣ.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r6.claim: Naml reports the blessing spoken at the call; al-Qaṣaṣ instead specifies the place from which the call came.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r6.anchor: {نُودِيَ أَن بُورِكَ} {نُودِيَ مِن شَاطِىءِ الوادي الأيمن}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r7.claim: The Naml account includes a glorification of God at the call that is absent from al-Qaṣaṣ.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p106/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p106/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p106/r1.claim: Naml alone includes the blessing over those in and around the fire and God's glorification, fitting its scene of exaltation; the utterance honors the Lord of the worlds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p106/r1.anchor: الموقف في النمل موقفُ تعظيمٍ كما أسلفنا وهذا القول تعظيم لله رب العالمين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r3.claim: Returning to the Musa narratives, the author notes that Naml uses jāʾahā and al-Qaṣaṣ uses atāhā, applying the heavier-versus-lighter contrast to their wording.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p104/r3.anchor: ونعود إلى ما نحن فيه من قصة موسى، فقد قال في سورة النمل: {فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا} وقال في سورة القصص: {فَلَمَّآ أَتَاهَا}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p86/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p86/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p86/r3.claim: Although Qasas says “Lord of the worlds,” Naml also says it and then adds “the Mighty, the Wise”; this clarifies the difference between the two settings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p86/r3.anchor: وقد قال ذلك أيضا في النمل، فقد قال: "وسبحان الله ربّ العالمين" وزاد عليه: "إنّهُ أنا الله العَزيزُ الحَكيمُ"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p69/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p69/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p69/r1.claim: Prompted by a reader’s observation that Moses’ narratives in al-Naml and al-Qaṣaṣ closely resemble one another, he set out to explain their wording differences, including these paired expressions.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p69/r1.anchor: من نحو قوله تعالى: "فلما جاءها نودي" و "فلما أتاها نودي"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r1.claim: The comparison sets Qasas’s geographic detail, family instruction, and hopeful ‘perhaps I will bring’ against Naml’s shorter, definite ‘I will bring.’

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r2.claim: Qasas asks for a jadwa of fire; Naml speaks of bringing a shihab qabas.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r3.claim: Qasas says ‘when he reached it’ and specifies the call’s location; Naml uses ‘came to it,’ adds the blessing and glorification, and omits the place detail.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r4.claim: Qasas uses ‘an ya Musa’ and names God as Lord of the worlds; Naml directly addresses Musa and names God the Mighty, Wise.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p70/r5.claim: Other contrasts include inserting versus passing the hand, two proofs versus nine signs, Qasas’s wing gesture, and Pharaoh’s people versus his elite.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r1.claim: Naml adds the blessing formula, absent from Qasas, because this scene is one of glorifying God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r1.anchor: الموقف في النمل موقف تعظيم كما أسلفنا وهذا القول تعظيم لله رب العالمين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r2.claim: Naml directly calls Musa to honor him; Qasas uses explanatory an because its scene does not carry the same honorific force.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r2.anchor: فشرفه بالنداء المباشر في حين ليس المقام كذلك في القصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r3.claim: In Qasas, an is explicative: the call means ‘in words or a sign conveying this meaning,’ unlike an explicit quoted utterance; the author compares 37:104–105 and 11:46.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r3.anchor: فالأول معناه: أشرت إليه بالذهاب، بأي لفظ أو دلالة تدل على هذا المعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r4.claim: Qasas’s more expansive, detailed mode suits adding an before the call.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r4.anchor: المقام في سورة القصص مقام تبسط وتفصيل فجاء بـ (أن) زيادة في التبسط

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r5.claim: The weightier commission in Naml calls for a direct summons.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r5.anchor: ثقل التكليف في النمل يستدعي المباشرة في النداء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r6.claim: Naml’s pronoun of شأن in ‘innahu ana’ and the names al-Aziz al-Hakim add exaltation; Qasas instead says ‘inni ana Allah rabb al-alamin.’
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p85/r6.anchor: فجاء بضمير الشأن الدال على التعظيم في آية النمل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r1.claim: A jadwa may or may not be a borrowed flame; the shihab qabas gives greater benefit and signals steadiness and courage. He places the ember in the fearful setting and the flame in the other setting.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r1.anchor: الجذوة قد تكون قبسا وغير قبس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r2.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r2.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes atyan as an easy coming and says maji is broader because atyan specifically implies ease.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r2.anchor: قال الراغب الأصفهاني مفرقا بين الإتيان والمجيء: الإتيان مجيءٌ بسهولة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r3.claim: Lexicons usually define the two verbs by each other, but derivatives of atā indicate ease, as in an easy road and water channels made easy.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r3.anchor: غير أنهم يذكرون في بعض تصريفات (أتى) ما يدل على السهولة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r4.claim: The Qur’an uses jā’a for difficulty or greater hardship than atā, as in 23:27, 50:19, and 18:71, 18:74.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p75/r4.anchor: والذي استبان لي أن القرآن الكريم يستعمل المجيء لما فيه صعوبة ومشقة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r1.claim: Musa’s Naml promise is firmer than his Qasas hope, and bringing a bright, borrowed flame is harder than bringing an ember; these make Naml’s situation more arduous.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r1.anchor: ما قطعه موسى على نفسه في النمل أصعب مما في القصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r2.claim: Naml’s commission to Pharaoh and his people is broader and harder than Qasas’s commission to Pharaoh and his elite, since the people are dispersed and varied.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r2.anchor: وتبليغ القوم أوسع وأصعب من تبليغ الملأ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r3.claim: The Taha account, where Musa is sent to Pharaoh alone, says ‘ataha’; this supports the lighter verb in a less demanding setting.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r4.claim: Because the Naml circumstances are harder, it uses jā’a rather than the lighter atā.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r4.anchor: فجاء بالفعل (جاء) دون (أتى) الذي هو أخف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r5.claim: Qasas gives the direction and setting of the call for its detailed mode; Naml’s mode is concise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p84/r5.anchor: موطن القصص موطن تفصيل، وموطن النمل موطن إيجاز كما ذكرت

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r1.claim: The root d-kh-l and its derivatives occur five times in Naml, at 27:12, 18, 19, 34, and 44, but not in Qasas, which suits Naml’s use of ‘insert.’
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r1.anchor: إن الفعل (دخل) ومشتقاته تكرر خمس مرات (انظر الآيات 12، 18، 19، 34، 44) في النمل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r2.claim: Idkhal is narrower than suluk: suluk may mean traversing or inserting, while idkhal specifically means insertion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r2.anchor: الإدخال أخص من السلك أو السلوك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r3.claim: Suluk can be easy and effortless, as in the bee following gentle paths and water entering springs; insertion is harder and suits the difficult commission.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r3.anchor: فناسب وضع السلوك في موطن السهولة واليسر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r4.claim: Suluk fits the fearful setting, whereas idkhal fits security and confidence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r4.anchor: وناسب أن يوضع السلوك في مقام الخوف، وأن يوضع لإدخال في مقام الأمن والثقة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r5.claim: The more specific idkhal matches the specific shihab qabas; the broader suluk matches the broader jadwa.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r5.anchor: وناسب أن يوضع الإدخال وهو أخص من السلوك مع (الشهاب القبس)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r6.claim: Qasas adds the wing gesture because fear recurs in that story and the surah gives a fuller account.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r6.anchor: (الرهب) هو الخوف، وهو مناسب لجو الخوف الذي تردد في القصة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r7.claim: The comparison notes that Naml says ‘among nine signs,’ while Qasas says ‘those two proofs.’
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p90/r7.anchor: قال في النمل: "في تسعِ آياتٍ" وقال في القصص: "فذانِكَ بُرهانانِ"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p783/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p783/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p783/r3.claim: Taha uses atyan more than fifteen times and maji four; Naml uses maji eight times and atyan thirteen, fitting their respective verb choices here.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p783/r3.anchor: تكرر لفظ الإتيان أكثر من 15 مرة والمجيء 4 مرات

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r9.claim: The passive verb leaves the caller and source of the voice ambiguous, while magnifying the event.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r9.anchor: The passive mood of the verb

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r10.claim: The apparent fire is a veil of light behind which God's blessed being is with the blessed angels; it is not an ordinary fire.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r10.anchor: this is not fire: behind the veil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p467/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p467/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p467/r1.claim: The announcement of blessing familiarizes and reassures Moses: an unexpected voice in the dark valley could frighten him, but its source and message signal no danger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p467/r1.anchor: this phase was very essential for Moses (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p467/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p467/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p467/r2.claim: The glorification rules out false notions of God: He is free of defects, and Moses should trust His merciful providence, since the Lord of all worlds controls everything.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p467/r2.anchor: God, Lord of the worlds, is free of all defects and shortcomings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r1.claim: The preceding verses prepare Moses mentally and emotionally for his mission; the following material gives signs essential for confronting Pharaoh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p468/r1.anchor: The previous verses guide Moses (sws) regarding the mental and emotional preparation for the mission at hand.

NASHR:v2p26#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p26#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p26#2/r1.claim: Before bāʾ, a sākin nūn or tanwin becomes a pure mīm without assimilation, with ghunna; the converted mīm is hidden. There is no disagreement on this, and reported disagreement confuses it with sākin mīm before bāʾ.
NASHR:v2p26#2/r1.anchor: فإن النون الساكنة والتنوين يقلبان عندها ميما خالصة من غير إدغام

NASHR:v2p26#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p26#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p26#2/r2.claim: The sound of أن بورك is thus indistinguishable from the hidden mīm in يعتصم بالله; al-Dani’s reported disagreement concerns sākin mīm, not the converted mīm.
NASHR:v2p26#2/r2.anchor: فلا فرق حينئذ في اللفظ بين أن بورك، وبين: يعتصم بالله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#2/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the blessed presence in the fire as the light of God.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ نودي أن بورك من في النار ﴾ قال نور الله بورك

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
