ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the fire was light and those around it were angels.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p79#2/r2.anchor: قال الحسن هو النور ومن حوله الملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r1.claim: The pronoun most naturally refers to the fire Moses had said he perceived; the alternative that it refers to the tree is judged implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r1.anchor: أي النار التي قال فيها ( إني ءانست نارا )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r2.claim: Moses was called from the side of the mountain.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r2.anchor: أي موسى عليه السلام من جانب الطور ( أن بورك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r3.claim: Alusi prefers أن as explanatory, since the call carries the sense of speech without explicit words of quotation.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r3.anchor: معناه أي بورك على أن أن مفسرة لما في النداء من معنى القول دون حروفه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r4.claim: Some allow reduced أن with an implicit pronoun of the matter, though objectors say a verb must be separated from it by قد, a future particle, or negation; replies note that the rule has exceptions, including a supplicatory verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تكون أن المخففة من الثقيلة واسمها ضمير الشأن ومنعه بعضهم لعدم الفصل بينها وبين الفعل بقد أو السين أو سوف أو حرف النفي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r5.speaker: الرضى
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r5.claim: Al-Radi argues that if بورك is a supplication, أن must be explanatory because the reduced heavy particle cannot, by consensus, precede a performative; Alusi says the claimed consensus is unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r5.anchor: وادعى الرضى أن بورك إذا جعل دعاء فان مفسرة لاغير لأن المخففة لايقع بعدها فعل إنشائي إجماعا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r6.claim: Another analysis makes أن a verbal noun particle, with بورك either a predicate or an optative construction; Alusi notes disagreement about whether nominalization loses the request meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المصدرية الناصبة للافعال و ( بورك ) حينئذ اما خبر أو إنشاء للدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r7.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r7.claim: Al-Kashf objects that the verbal-noun reading would not make بورك good news, while the opening announces Moses' great commission and the blessing it will spread through Syria; Alusi questions this objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r7.anchor: وفي الكشف يمنع عن جعلها مصدرية عدم سداد المعنى لأن ( بورك ) إذ ذاك ليس يصلح بشارة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r8.claim: On either analysis, the preposition is omitted in نودي بأن; the attached phrase is not the passive agent, which is most naturally the pronoun referring to Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r8.anchor: وعلى الوجهين الكلام على حذف حرف الجر أي نودي بأن الخ والجار والمجرور متعلق بما عنده وليس نائب الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r9.claim: Another parsing makes the attached phrase the passive agent; a further view takes the agent pronoun to denote the call itself, interpreted by what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r9.anchor: وقيل : هو نائب الفاعل ولا ضمير

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r10.claim: Alusi takes بورك as a predicate from blessing, while another gloss here is “sanctified and purified, and increased in good.”
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r10.anchor: والأظهر في الضمير رجوعه لموسى وفي أن أنها مفسرة وفي ( بورك ) أنه خبر وهو من البركة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r11.speaker: جماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r11.claim: A group supplies an omitted “place” twice: those in the place of the fire and around it, the blessed plot named in 28:30; Ubayy's reading says “the earth and those around it.”
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r11.anchor: ذهب جماعة إلى أن في الكلام مضافا مقدرا في موضعين أي من في مكان النار ومن حول مكانها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r12.claim: Alusi favors including everyone in the valley and nearby blessed Syrian land, homeland and resting place of prophets, especially the spot where God spoke to Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r12.anchor: واستظهر عموم من لكل ( من ) في ذلك الوادي وحواليه من أرض الشام الموسومة بالبركات

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r13.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r13.claim: Ubayy's reported reading تباركت الأرض supports interpreting the phrase as a blessed place.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r13.anchor: وتدل على ذلك قراءة أبي ( تباركت الأرض ومن حولها )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r14.claim: One view identifies the one in the fire as Moses and those around it as attending angels, supported by a version adding “of the angels,” transmitted from Ubayy, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ikrima; many classify it as commentary, not a canonical reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r14.anchor: وقيل : من في النار موسى عليه السلام ومن حولها الملائكة الحاضرون عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r15.claim: Another view reverses the referents, taking the first group as angels and the second as Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r15.anchor: وقيل : الأول الملائكة والثاني موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r16.claim: Some avoid supplying an omitted noun by treating spatial “in” as figurative for nearness; they choose Moses for the first referent and angels for those around him, while the passage blesses Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p160/r16.anchor: واستغنى بعضهم عن تقدير المضاف بجعل الظرفية مجازا عن القرب التام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r1.claim: The glorification may express Moses' amazement, signal that God intends and brings about a momentous affair through His nurturing of the worlds, or inform Moses of God's transcendence.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r1.anchor: تعجيب له عليه السلام من ذلك وإيذان بأن ذلك مريده ومكونه رب العالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r2.claim: Alternatively, it informs Moses of God's transcendence so that hearing divine speech does not suggest resemblance to human speech, or it commands Moses to glorify God.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r2.anchor: أو خبر له عليه السلام بتنزيهه سبحانه لئلا يتوهم من سماع كلامه تعالى التشبيه بما للبشر أو طلب منه عليه السلام لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r3.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses uttered the glorification after hearing the call from the tree, declaring God free of the attributes of created beings.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r3.anchor: وقال السدي : هو من كلام موسى عليه السلام قاله لما سمع النداء من الشجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r4.speaker: ابن شجرة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r4.claim: Ibn Shajara takes the words as God's speech meaning “blessed is whoever glorifies God”; Alusi says this is far from the apparent wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r4.anchor: وقال ابن شجرة : هو من كلام الله تعالى ومعناه وبورك من سبح الله تعالى رب العالمين وهذا بعيد من دلالة اللفظ جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r5.claim: A further view addresses the Prophet Muhammad with a command to glorify God, parenthetically between the preceding statement and what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p161/r5.anchor: وقيل : هو خطاب لنبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم مراد به التنزيه وجعل معترضا بين ما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r1.speaker: البخاري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r1.claim: Al-Bukhari reports that God gathers people and calls in a voice heard equally by those far away and those near: I am the King, the Judge.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r1.anchor: يحشر الله العباد فيناديهم بصوت يسمعه من بعدكما يسمعه من قرب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the blessed one in the fire as God Himself: the Lord of the worlds’ light was in the tree; another report says God was in the light and called from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r2.anchor: يعني تبارك وتعالى نفسه كان نور رب العالمين في الشجرة وفي رواية عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r3.speaker: مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r3.claim: Muslim transmits two descriptions of God’s veil: it is light in one report and fire in another.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r3.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم حجابه النور وفي رواية له حجابه النار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r4.claim: For mystics, God can disclose Himself as He wills without being confined by appearances; His absolute transcendence remains even in manifestation, resolving difficulties about divine appearance in a form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r4.anchor: وأنه منزه في تجليه قريب في تعاليه لا تقيده المظاهر عند أرباب الأذواق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r5.claim: Al-Alusi reads the glorification as denying that God is confined to the image, location, or direction from which He calls; manifestation does not limit the Lord of the worlds.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r5.anchor: أي عن التقييد بالصورة والمكان والجهة وإن ناداك منها لكونه موصوفا بصفة رب العالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r6.claim: He explains that divine might precludes limitation while divine wisdom calls for disclosure in the requested fire-form; Moses therefore heard God’s letters and sound directly, behind the fire’s veil, through divine light manifested there.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r6.anchor: فالمسموع على هذا صوت وحرف سمعهما موسى عليه السلام من الله تعالى المتجلي بنوره في مظهر النار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r7.speaker: الأشعري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says the common attribution to al-Ashari that Moses actually heard inner speech is mistaken; al-Ashari allowed such hearing as a possibility, not what occurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r7.anchor: وأما ما شاع عن الأشعري من القول بسماع الكلام النفسي القائم بذات الله تعالى فهو من باب التجويز والإمكان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r8.claim: The sacred hadith about God becoming a beloved servant’s hearing shows how, through luminous self-disclosure, the servant may extraordinarily hear nonmaterial speech while remaining within the principle of 42:11.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r8.anchor: كنت سمعه الذي يسمع به الحديث ومن الواضح أن الله تبارك وتعالى إذا كان بتجليه النوري

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r9.speaker: الماتريدي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r9.claim: Al-Maturidi also permits extraordinary hearing of what is not sound, according to al-Tabṣira; Ibn al-Humam’s report of impossibility refers only to ordinary impossibility, so there is no substantive disagreement between the two imams.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r9.anchor: والإمام الماتريدي أيضا يجوز سماع ما ليس بصوت على وجه خرق العادة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r10.speaker: الأشعري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r10.claim: Al-Alusi explains that during recitation what is directly heard is the reciter’s verbal speech; its letters are forms of God’s hidden essential speech, which is thereby heard through the form and only heard directly by supernatural means.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r10.anchor: المسموع أو لا وبالذات عند التلاوة إنما هو الكلام اللفظي الذي حروفه عارضة لصوت القاريء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r11.speaker: الباقلاني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r11.claim: Al-Baqillani’s claim that one hears recitation rather than what is recited can mean only that the verbal utterance is heard directly, leaving no real disagreement on Al-Alusi’s reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p17/r11.anchor: إنما تسمع التلاوة دون المتلو والقراءة دون المقروء يمكن حمله على أنه أراد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r12.claim: The idiom means God blessed whoever was in or over the fire; Arabic uses blessing someone, in someone, and upon someone equivalently.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r12.anchor: أي: بورك على من في النار أو من في النار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r13.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r13.claim: One view refers the blessing to Moses, who sought the fire, and the angels around it; it is God's greeting of blessing to Moses, like the greeting to Abraham's household.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r13.anchor: وقال قوم: البركة راجعة إلى موسى والملائكة، معناه: بورك في من طلب النار، وهو موسى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r14.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r14.claim: Most exegetes say the fire was actually light, called fire because Moses thought it was fire; angels in the light praised God aloud.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r14.anchor: ومذهب أكثر المفسرين أن المراد بالنار النور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r1.claim: Those around the light were Moses, who was near it but not inside it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r1.anchor: و"من حولها" هو موسى لأنه كان بالقرب منها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r2.claim: One view identifies both those in and around the fire as angels.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r2.anchor: وقيل: "من في النار ومن حولها" جميعا الملائكة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r3.claim: Another view identifies Moses as in the fire and angels around it; being near a place can be described as reaching it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r3.anchor: وقيل: "من في النار" موسى و"من حولها" الملائكة، وموسى وإن لم يكن في النار كان قريبا منها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r4.claim: Some say the blessing refers to the fire itself; Mujahid transmits Ibn Abbas's statement that it was blessed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن البركة راجعة إلى النار. وروى مجاهد عن ابن عباس أنه قال: معناه بوركت النار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr transmits Ibn Abbas's report that Ubayy read an-būrikat al-nāru, explicitly blessing the fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r5.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: سمعت أبيا يقرأ: أن بوركت النار ومن حولها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r6.claim: Min can mean mā, as in 24:45; mā can be extra, as in 38:11, giving the sense that the fire and those around it, Moses and angels, were blessed as was the blessed place.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r6.anchor: و"من" قد تأتي بمعنى ما، كقوله تعالى: "فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r7.claim: They interpret the one in the fire as God, sanctified there: He called Moses from that direction and made him hear His speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r7.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والحسن في قوله: {بورك من في النار} يعني قدس من في النار، وهو الله، عنى به نفسه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r8.claim: A Torah passage says God came from Sinai, appeared from Seir, and rose from Paran; the author associates these with Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, and identifies Paran with Mecca.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r8.anchor: كما روي: أنه مكتوب في التوراة: "جاء الله من سيناء، وأشرف من ساعين، واستعلى من جبال فاران"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r9.claim: Another view says what Moses saw was God's light.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r9.anchor: قيل: كان ذلك نوره عز وجل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r10.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says it was literal fire and one of God's veils; a hadith says uncovering the veil would burn creation reached by His sight.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r10.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كانت النار بعينها، والنار إحدى حجب الله تعالى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r11.claim: God declares Himself exalted above every evil and defect.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p145/r11.anchor: ثم نزه الله نفسه وهو المنزه من كل سوء وعيب

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r2.claim: Because the call carries the force of speech, أن بورك can be rendered simply بورك; alternatively أن is a verbal noun particle or a light form of أنّ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r2.anchor: فإن النداء فيه معنى القول، أو ب { أن بورك } على أنها مصدرية

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r3.claim: Although a light أنّ normally requires a compensatory لا، قد، سـ، or سوف, this is a supplication and differs from ordinary cases.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r3.anchor: والتخفيف وإن اقتضى التعويض بلا أو قد أو السين أو سوف لكنه دعاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r4.claim: The apparent referent is everyone in that land, the valley, and its surroundings in Syria, blessed as the abode and burial place of prophets, especially the place where God spoke to Moses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r4.anchor: والظاهر أنه عام في كل من تلك الأرض، وفي ذلك الواد وحواليها من أرض الشام الموسومة بالبركات

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r5.claim: An alternative interpretation identifies those in and around the fire as Moses and the angels who were present.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد موسى والملائكة الحاضرون، وتصدير الخطاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r6.claim: The opening address gives glad tidings that a momentous affair has been decreed whose blessing will spread through Syria.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r6.anchor: بشارة بأنه قد قضى له أمر عظيم تنتشر بركته في أقطار الشأم

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r7.claim: The glorification is part of the call, guarding listeners from imagining that hearing God's speech implies likeness between God and creation, and expressing wonder at the affair's greatness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r7.anchor: لئلا يتوهم من سماع كلامه تشبيها وللتعجيب من عظمة ذلك الأمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r8.claim: Alternatively, Moses himself exclaimed in wonder at the greatness of what had happened.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r8.anchor: أو تعجب من موسى لما دهاه من عظمته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r5.claim: The object Moses reached was what he had taken to be a fire.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r6.claim: The call is expressed in the passive, with God as the caller.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r7.claim: The unspecified call first creates suspense; the clarification directs the hearer to infer the greatness of the event.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r7.anchor: ولما كان البيان بعد الإبهام أعظم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r8.claim: The wording signals that the call is clarified by what follows because calling here has the force of saying.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r9.claim: To bless is to establish flourishing that brings increase, purity, and every describable good.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r9.anchor: أي ثبت تثبيتا يحصل منه من النماء والطهارة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r10.claim: The phrase may refer to the fire’s location or to the person seeking it, with the latter functioning as supplication.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r10.anchor: أي بقعتها , أو طلبها وهو طلب بمعنى الدعاء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r11.claim: The account suggests a large tree: as Moses approached, the fire moved away and he followed it into the ravine, where light surrounded him; the light is called fire after his first impression.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r11.anchor: العبارة تدل على أن الشجرة كانت كبيرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r12.claim: The radiance, though called fire, may have been light because Moses first thought he saw fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r12.anchor: وسمي النور نارا على ما كان في ظن موسى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r13.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the fire was actual, as Moses saw it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r13.anchor: سعيد بن جبير : بل كانت نارا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r14.claim: The cited hadith says God’s veil is fire, and if He uncovered it, the splendors of His face would burn whatever His sight reaches.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r14.anchor: كما في الحديث : ( حجابه النار لو كشفها لأحرقت سبحات وجهه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r15.claim: Those around the fire include all angels and the sacred lands, then and whenever God wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r15.anchor: من جميع الملائكة عليهم السلام وتلك الأراضي المقدسة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r16.claim: The sacred lands deserve this status because prophets were sent there, revelation descended there, and prophets were laid to rest there.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r16.anchor: لأنها مبعث الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام ومهبط الوحي عليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r17.claim: The call came from every direction and Moses heard it through all his senses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r17.anchor: من جميع الجهات , فسمعه بجميع الحواس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r18.claim: The context implies a command to rejoice at this great glad tiding and glorify the perfectly complete King in a manner befitting His majesty.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r18.anchor: أي ونزه الملك الذي له الكمال المطلق تنزيها يليق بجلاله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r19.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is a predicate coordinated with “blessed”: God is transcendent and is not located at the place of the call or anywhere else.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r19.anchor: أي وتنزه الله سبحانه تنزها يليق بجلاله عن أن يكون في موضع النداء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r20.claim: Calling God Lord of the worlds shows He deserves sanctification through His perfect essence and acts toward creatures, including raising Moses as an adult after raising him as a child.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r20.anchor: التي منها ما يريد أن يربي به موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام كبيرا بعد ما رباه به صغيرا

DURR-FULL:v6p340/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p340/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p340/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the Blessed One in the fire is God Himself; the light of the Lord of the worlds was in the tree and the surrounding ones were angels.
DURR-FULL:v6p340/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك من في النار} يعني تبارك وتعالى نفسه

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the fire was light, and glosses the phrase as blessing upon the one in the fire and those around it.
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: كانت تلك النار نورا {أن بورك من في النار ومن} حول النار

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the phrase as the fire itself being blessed.
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أن بورك من في النار} قال: بوركت النار

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r3.claim: Mujahid gives the same gloss: the fire was blessed.

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r4.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb's codex reads the fire as blessed; Qatada reports that the fire is God's light and those around it are angels.
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قال: في مصحف أبي بن كعب (بوركت النار ومن حولها) أما النار فيزعمون أنها نور رب العالمين

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r5.claim: ʿIkrima recited the wording with the fire explicitly feminine: blessed be the fire.
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه كان يقرأ (أن بوركت النار)

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r6.claim: Muhammad b. Kaʿb identifies the fire as the Light of the Merciful and those around it as Moses and the angels.
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب في الآية قال: النار: نور الرحمن {ومن حولها} موسى والملائكة

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r7.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r7.claim: Al-Suddi explains the word as meaning sanctified.
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r7.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {بورك} قال: قدس

DURR-FULL:v6p341/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r8.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r8.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet saying God does not sleep, raises and lowers the balance, receives deeds of night and day in turn, and is veiled by light; lifting the veil would burn all reached by His sight; Abu ʿUbayda then recited this verse.
DURR-FULL:v6p341/r8.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: قام فينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن الله لا ينام ولا ينبغي له أن ينام

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843#2/r1.speaker: وهب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843#2/r1.claim: Wahb recounts Moses approaching a fire on a green tree; it became a column of brilliant light, and God called to him from above and identified Himself as the speaker.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843#2/r1.anchor: سمعت وهبا يقول : لما راى موسى النار انطلق يسير حتى وقف منها قريبا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r1.claim: The Prophet says God neither sleeps nor should sleep, lowers and raises the balance, and receives the deeds of night and day in turn.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ان الله لا ينام ولا ينبغي له ان ينام

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r2.speaker: المسعودي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r2.claim: Al-Masudi adds that God’s veil is fire and, if uncovered, the splendor of His face would burn everything reached by His sight.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r2.anchor: زاد المسعودي وحجابه النار لو كشفها حرقت سحابة وجهه كل شيء ادركه بصره

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda recited the verse after the report about the divine veil and fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r3.anchor: ثم قرا أبو عبيدة ان بورك من في النار ومن حولها .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “blessed” as “made holy” or “sanctified.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : بورك من في النار يقول : قدس .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r5.claim: Mujahid says the fire was blessed, adding that Ibn Abbas said the same.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ان بورك من في النار بوركت النار كذلك يقول ابن العباس .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says God was in the light and the call came from the light.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس فلما جاءها نودي ان بورك من في النار قال : الله في النور ، ونودي من النور .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas describes what was called fire as light, with blessing in the light and around the fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r7.anchor: عن يزيد النحوي ان عكرمة حدثه ، عن ابن عباس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the one in the fire is God Himself: the Lord of the worlds’ light was in the tree and around it.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2844/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس فلما جاءها نودي ان بورك من في النار يعني نفسه قال : كان نور رب العالمين في الشجرة ، ومن حولها .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the one in the fire as God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r1.anchor: عن سعيد ان بورك من في النار قال : الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r2.claim: Ikrima says God was in His light.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r2.anchor: ثنا أبو معاوية ، عن أبي شيبان ، عن عكرمة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Moses was called while God was in the light.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r3.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب ، عن سعيد بن جبير

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r4.claim: Qatada reports that Ubayy ibn Ka'b’s codex reads “Blessed be the fire and those around it.”
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ان بورك من في النار ومن حولها وهي في مصحف أبي بن كعب ان بوركت النار ومن حولها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r5.claim: Qatada reports the view that the fire was a light from God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r5.anchor: اما النار فيزعمون انها ضوء من الله عز وجل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r6.speaker: أبو صخر
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r6.claim: Abu Sakhr recounts the sheep repeatedly fleeing and Moses approaching; what appeared as fire was God’s light, with Moses around it.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r6.anchor: حدثنا أبو صخر فلما جاءها نودي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the fire was the Merciful’s light, a ray of God’s light, with Moses and angels around it.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب في قوله عز وجل : ان بورك من في النار ومن حولها قال : النار نور الرحيم ضوء من نور الله عز وجل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says angels were in the fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2845/r8.anchor: عن السدي ان بورك من في النار قال : كان في النار ملائكة .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those around the fire as angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومن حولها قال : الملائكة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r2.claim: Ikrima is also reported to identify those around it as angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r2.anchor: وروى عن عكرمة والحسن ، وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة مثل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r3.claim: Al-Hasan is also reported to identify those around it as angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r3.anchor: وروى عن عكرمة والحسن ، وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة مثل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr is also reported to identify those around it as angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r4.anchor: وروى عن عكرمة والحسن ، وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة مثل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r5.claim: Qatada is also reported to identify those around it as angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r5.anchor: وروى عن عكرمة والحسن ، وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة مثل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r6.speaker: أبو صخر
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r6.claim: Abu Sakhr again describes the scene as God’s light, with Moses around the light.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r6.anchor: حدثني أبو صخر ان بورك من في النار ومن حولها قال : كان نور الله عز وجل وهو الذي كان في ذلك النور

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses, startled by the call, glorified the Lord of the worlds; the voice then addressed him as God, Lord of the worlds.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2846/r7.anchor: عن السدي ان بورك من في النار ومن حولها فلما سمع موسى النداء فزع فقال : سبحان الله رب العالمين نودي : يا موسى اني انا الله رب العالمين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r8.claim: The fire appeared only to Moses because it was an otherworldly light shown to him, not an ordinary fire; the emphatic إن suggests his wife doubted its appearance since she could not see it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r8.anchor: ولم تظهر النار إلا لموسى دون غيره من أهله لأنها لم تكن نارا معتادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r8.claim: The feminine pronoun in جاءها follows the earlier naming of the light as fire, based on how it appeared to Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r8.anchor: جريا على ما تقدم من تسمية النور نارا بحسب ما لاح لموسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r9.claim: The blessing or sanctification here captures part of the instruction to remove one's sandals at the sacred valley in 20:12; baraka here means sanctified and purified.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r9.anchor: هو بعض ما اقتضاه قوله في طه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r10.claim: The verb baraka can be transitive, as in باركك الله, meaning that God made blessing for someone; compare its use at 3:96 and 11:48.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r11.claim: The particle أن is explanatory after نودي because that verb already implies speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r11.anchor: تفسيرية لفعل { نودي } لأن فيه معنى القول دون حروفه

IBNHIBBAN:946/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:946/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNHIBBAN:946/r1.claim: Saʿd reports that a Bedouin asks for devotional words; the Prophet teaches monotheism, magnification, praise and the verse's glorification formula, then asks forgiveness, mercy, guidance and provision.
IBNHIBBAN:946/r1.anchor: مصعب بن سعد بن أبي وقاص، عن أبيه

IBNHIBBAN:946/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:946/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNHIBBAN:946/r2.claim: Abu Hatim says requests for guidance mean asking to remain steadfast and increase in guidance, since a believer has already been guided.
IBNHIBBAN:946/r2.anchor: قال أبو حاتم رضي الله عنه: كل ما في هذه الأخبار: اللهم اهدني

IBNMAJAH:196/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:196/r1.speaker: النبي
IBNMAJAH:196/r1.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet's description of God's light and that God neither sleeps nor should sleep; Abu Ubayda then cites this verse after the report.
IBNMAJAH:196/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي مُوسَى، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَنَامُ وَلاَ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَنَامَ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r8.claim: As Moses approached, he saw fire in a green samur tree that did not burn; it seemed to recede as he drew near, and was divine light rather than fire itself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r8.anchor: فلما دنا منها رأى النار في شجرة سمر خضراء وهي لا تحرقها، وكلما قرب هو منها بعدت هي منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r9.claim: God called Moses from the direction of the tree and made him hear His speech; Moses had hoped the fire would provide directions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r9.anchor: وكان ذلك نورا من نور الله عز وجل ولم يكن نارا في نفسها لكن ظنه موسى نارا فناداه الله عز وجل عند ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r1.claim: When Moses approached what he thought was a fire, he was actually approaching light.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r1.anchor: أي جاء موسى النار وإنما كان نورا فاعتقده نارا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan take the phrase to mean that God, who is holy, is in the fire; Ibn al-Jawzī clarifies that it means the one calling from the fire is holy, not that God indwells anything.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r2.anchor: قدس من في النار وهو الله عز وجل قاله ابن عباس والحسن والمعنى قدس من ناداه من النار لا أن الله عز وجل يحل في شيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r3.claim: Mujāhid treats min as extra, yielding the sense “the fire was blessed.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r3.anchor: زائدة والمعنى بوركت النار قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the phrase as a blessing upon the one in or near the fire, with an omitted complement referring to Moses seeking the fire; Arabic permits blessing someone, upon him, or in him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r4.anchor: المعنى بورك على من في النار أوفيمن في النار قال الفراء والعرب تقول باركه الله وبارك عليه وبارك فيه بمعنى واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r5.claim: This blessing is a greeting from God to Moses, like the angels' greeting of blessing to Abraham at 11:73.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r5.anchor: وهذه تحية من الله تعالى لموسى بالبركة كما حيا إبراهيم بالبركة على ألسنة الملائكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan say those around the fire are the angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r6.anchor: أحدها الملائكة قاله ابن عباس والحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says those around the fire are Moses and the angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r7.anchor: والثاني موسى والملائكة قاله محمد بن كعب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r8.claim: A third view refers to Moses alone: the blessing is upon the person seeking the fire who is near it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p155/r8.anchor: والثالث موسى فالمعنى بورك فيمن يطلبها وهو قريب منها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir frames the passage as a reminder of God choosing and speaking privately to Moses, giving him striking signs, and sending him to Pharaoh's elite, who rejected them arrogantly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r1.anchor: مذكرا له ما كان من أمر موسى، كيف اصطفاه الله وكلمه، وناجاه وأعطاه من الآيات العظيمة الباهرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r5.claim: His prediction came true: he returned with momentous news and took from the fire a great light.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r5.anchor: وكان كما قال، فإنه رجع منها بخبر عظيم، واقتبس منها نورا عظيما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r6.claim: At the site Moses saw a tremendous sight: fire flared in a green tree without consuming its greenery, and its light reached the sky.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r6.anchor: والنار تضطرم في شجرة خضراء، لا تزداد النار إلا توقدا، ولا تزداد الشجرة إلا خضرة ونضرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and others report that what Moses saw was not fire but a glowing light.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: لم تكن نارا، إنما كانت نورا (4) يتوهج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies the light as the light of the Lord of the worlds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r8.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس: نور رب العالمين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the blessing as sanctification.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, Said ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, and Qatada say those around the fire were angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r1.anchor: {ومن حولها} أي: من الملائكة. قاله ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، والحسن، وقتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r2.claim: Abu Musa reports that the Prophet said God does not sleep, controls the balance, and receives the deeds of night and day in turn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله لا ينام، ولا ينبغي له أن ينام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r3.speaker: المسعودي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r3.claim: Al-Masudi adds that God's veil is light or fire; if uncovered, the radiance of His face would burn everything His sight reaches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r3.anchor: زاد المسعودي: "وحجابه النور -أو النار -لو كشفها لأحرقت سبحات وجهه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda recited this verse after the report; Ibn Kathir says its underlying hadith is recorded in Sahih Muslim from Amr ibn Murra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r4.anchor: ثم قرأ أبو عبيدة: {أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that the underlying report is also transmitted in Sahih Muslim through Amr ibn Murra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179#2/r5.anchor: وأصل هذا الحديث مخرج في الصحيح لمسلم، من حديث عمرو بن مرة، به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r1.claim: God acts as He wills, resembles no creature, is not encompassed by His creations, and is exalted, unique, self-sufficient, and unlike created things; neither earth nor heavens contain Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p180/r1.anchor: ولا يشبه شيئا من مخلوقاته، ولا يحيط به شيء من مصنوعاته، وهو العلي العظيم، المباين لجميع المخلوقات

MUSNAD-AHMAD:19587/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19587/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19587/r1.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet's teaching that God does not sleep and that His radiant face is screened by fire; Abu Ubayda immediately recites 27:8, linking that description to its scene of the blessed fire.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19587/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الله عز وجل لا ينام، ولا ينبغي له أن ينام

JISHUMI:v8p5409/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r3.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r3.claim: Baraka is the establishment of growing good in something; al-Farra notes Arab expressions “May God bless you” and “bless you in it.”
JISHUMI:v8p5409/r3.anchor: البركة: ثبوت الخير النامي بالشيء، قال الفراء: العرب تقول: باركك الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r1.claim: أن is explanatory because the call contains the sense of speech: he was told, “Be blessed.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r1.anchor: { أن } هي المفسرة : لأن النداء فيه معنى القول . والمعنى : قيل له بورك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r2.claim: أن cannot be the lightened إنّ with an omitted pronoun of شأن, because that construction requires قد, an unelidable particle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r2.anchor: والضمير ضمير الشأن ؟ قلت : لا ، لأنه لا بد من ( قد ) . فإن قلت : فعلى إضمارها ؟ قلت : لا يصح ؛ لأنها علامة لا تحذف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r3.claim: The phrase blesses whoever is in the place of the fire and around it: the blessed spot by the valley's right bank in 28:30.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى { بورك من فى النار ومن حولها } بورك من في مكان النار ، ومن حول مكانها . ومكانها : البقعة التي حصلت فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r4.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r4.claim: Ubayy's reading has تباركت الأرض ومن حولها.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r4.anchor: وتدل عليه قراءة أبي . ( تباركت الأرض ومن حولها ) .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r5.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r5.claim: Another reading attributed to Ubayy has بوركت النار.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r6.claim: The place was blessed by the religious event there: God spoke to Moses, appointed him prophet, and displayed miracles through him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r6.anchor: والذي بوركت له البقعة ، وبورك من فيها وحواليها حدوث أمر ديني فيها : وهو تكليم الله موسى واستنباؤه له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r7.claim: The apparent sense is general: everyone in that land, valley, and vicinity of Syria, marked by blessings as the home of prophets and revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r7.anchor: والظاهر أنه عام في كل من كان في تلك الأرض وفي تلك الوادي وحواليهما من أرض الشام ،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r8.speaker: some
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r8.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the blessed ones to be Moses and the angels present.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالمبارك فيهم : موسى والملائكة الحاضرون .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r9.claim: The opening blessing tells Moses he has been chosen for an event whose blessing will spread throughout Syria.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r9.anchor: فما معنى ابتداء خطاب الله موسى بذلك عند مجيئه ؟ قلت : هي بشارة له بأنه قد قضى بأمر عظيم تنتشر منه في أرض الشام كلها البركة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r10.claim: The glorification expresses Moses' amazement and declares the Lord of all worlds wills and brings about this momentous event.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354#2/r10.anchor: { وسبحان الله رب العالمين } تعجيب لموسى عليه السلام من ذلك ، وإيذان بأن ذلك الأمر مريده ومكونه رب العالمين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r9.claim: Moses thought he had found fire, but what he encountered was light.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r9.anchor: يعني ظن أنها نار , وهي نور , قال وهب بن منبه : فلما رأى موسى وقف قريبا منها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r10.speaker: وهب بن منبه
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r10.claim: Wahb describes light and fire issuing from a very green al-ʿalayq tree; the flames grew while the tree grew greener, and when Moses approached to take a branch the fire leaned toward him and frightened him back until he understood it was commanded.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r10.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه : فلما رأى موسى وقف قريبا منها فرآها تخرج من فرع شجرة خضراء شديدة الخضرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses būrika as sanctified.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r11.anchor: أحدها : يعني قدس , قاله ابن عباس . الثاني : تبارك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r12.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r12.claim: Al-Naqqash glosses būrika as tabāraka, blessed.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r13.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r13.claim: Ibn Shajara locates the blessing in the fire itself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r13.anchor: الثالث : البركة في النار , حكاه ابن شجرة , وأنشد لعبد الله بن الزبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r1.claim: The preceding segment introduces a verse attributed to ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr as poetic evidence for the blessing language.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r1.anchor: فبورك في بنيك وفي بنيهم … إذا ذكروا ونحن لك الفداء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r2.claim: One view understands the fire as a fire containing light.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r2.anchor: وفي النار وجهان : أحدهما : أنها نار فيها نور .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r3.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r3.claim: The majority say it was light with no fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r3.anchor: ليس فيها نار , وهو قول الجمهور .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r4.claim: Mujahid reports a reading in Ubayy's codex, bōrikat al-nār, treating min as extra and making the fire itself the subject of blessing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r4.anchor: أحدها : بوركت النار , و { من } زيادة , وهي في مصحف أبي : { بوركت النار ومن حولها } قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r5.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r5.claim: Ibn ʿIsa says the blessed one in the fire is the light within it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r5.anchor: الثاني : بورك النور الذي في النار , قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r6.speaker: عكرمة وابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r6.claim: ʿIkrima and Ibn Jubayr identify the blessed one in the light as God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r6.anchor: الثالث : بورك الله الذي في النور , قاله عكرمة , وابن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r7.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r7.claim: Al-Suddi identifies those in the fire as angels.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r8.claim: Another view identifies the blessed one as the tree, which caught fire while remaining green and unburned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r8.anchor: الخامس : الشجرة لأن النار اشتعلت فيها وهي خضراء لا تحترق .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies those around the fire as angels.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r9.anchor: أحدهما : الملائكة , قاله ابن عباس . الثاني : موسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r10.speaker: أبو صخر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r10.claim: Abu Sakhr identifies the one around the fire as Moses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r11.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses uttered the glorification after hearing God's call, seeking God's aid and declaring Him transcendent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r11.anchor: أحدهما : أن موسى قال حين فرغ من سماع النداء من قوله الله : { سبحان الله رب العالمين } استعانة بالله وتنزيها له , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r12.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r12.claim: Ibn Shajara says God spoke these words, meaning that the one who glorifies the Lord of the worlds is blessed; they are part of the call to Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r12.anchor: الثاني : أن هذا من قول الله ومعناه : وبورك فيمن يسبح الله رب العالمين , حكاه ابن شجرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r13.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r13.claim: Al-Suddi says the call was God's speech from heaven at the tree.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r13.anchor: أحدهما : أنه كلام الله تعالى من السماء عند الشجرة وهو قول السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r14.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r14.claim: Al-Naqqash says God created speech in the tree, from which Moses heard it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r14.anchor: والثاني : أن الله خلق في الشجرة كلاما خرج منها حتى سمعه موسى , حكاه النقاش .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r15.speaker: وهب بن منبه
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r15.claim: Wahb reports that Moses did not touch a woman after God spoke to him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p195/r15.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه : ثم لم يمس موسى امرأة بعدما كلمه ربه .

MUJAHID:v2p469#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p469#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p469#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the fire was blessed and notes that Ibn ʿAbbas held the same view.
MUJAHID:v2p469#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ نودي أن بورك من في النار ﴾ قال بوركت النار قال مجاهد وكذلك قال ابن عباس

MUJAHID:v2p469#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p469#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p469#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the fire was blessed and that God called Moses while he was in the light.
MUJAHID:v2p469#2/r2.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ نودي أن بورك من في النار ﴾ قال يقول بوركت النار ناداه الله وهو في النور

MUQATIL:27:7-10/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r4.claim: What Moses reached was the fire, understood as the light of the Lord of Majesty.
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r4.anchor: { فلما جآءها } يعنى النار، وهو نور رب العزة، تبارك وتعالى

MUQATIL:27:7-10/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r5.claim: Those around the fire were angels; Muqatil identifies them as the blessed company in the call.
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r5.anchor: { نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها } يعنى الملائكة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r1.claim: The thing Moses came to was the fire he had seen.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r1.anchor: أي النار التي أبصرها نودى موسى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r2.claim: An may be the lightened form of anna: “he was called that blessed [is]”; the pronoun denotes the matter at hand. Although al-Zamakhshari disallows this without a compensating particle, the construction is permitted because a prayer has special rules.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r2.anchor: مخففة من الثقيلة وتقديره نودى بأن بورك والضمير ضمير الشان وجاز ذلك من غير عوض وإن منعه الزمخشري

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, an is explanatory because the call carries the sense of speech.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r3.anchor: ومفسرة لأن في النداء معنى القول

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r4.claim: Būrika means “was sanctified” or “was endowed with blessing and goodness.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r4.anchor: أي قدس أو جعل فيه البركة والخير

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r5.claim: Those in the place of the fire are the angels; the one around it is Moses, since a religious event occurred there: God spoke to and commissioned him and showed him miracles.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r5.anchor: أي بورك من في مكان النار وهم الملائكة ومن حول مكانها أي موسى لحدوث أمر ديني فيها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r6.claim: These words are part of the call and declare God transcendent of likeness and anything else unworthy of Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#3/r6.anchor: هو من جملة ما نودي فقد نزه ذاته عما لا يليق به من التشبيه وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r7.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r7.claim: Wahb says Moses came to what he thought was fire but was actually light.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فلما جاءها } أي فلما جاء موسى الذي ظن أنه نار وهي نور قاله وهب بن منبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r8.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r8.claim: Wahb describes fire issuing from a branch of a very green tree: the flame grew while the tree grew greener; Moses reached with a twig to take fire, recoiled when it leaned toward him, and remained bewildered until called.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r8.anchor: فلما رأى موسى النار وقف قريبا منها، فرآها تخرج من فرع شجرة خضراء شديدة الخضرة يقال لها العليق

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r9.claim: God called Moses, as in the account of calling him from the right side of the mountain.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r9.anchor: { نودي } أي ناداه الله كما قال: وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r10.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses أن as accusative, meaning “because”; he also allows nominative, making it the passive sentence’s subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج: { أن } في موضع نصب أي بأنه. قال: ويجوز أن تكون في موضع رفع جعلها اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r11.speaker: أبي وابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r11.claim: Abū Ḥātim reports a reading “أن بوركت النار”; al-Naḥḥās says its transmission is not sound, and if authentic it is exegetical, blessing the fire, angels, and Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r11.anchor: وحكى أبو حاتم أن في قراءة أبي وابن عباس ومجاهد { أن بوركت النار ومن حولها }. قال النحاس: ومثل هذا لا يوجد بإسناد صحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r12.speaker: الزجاج والثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r12.claim: Arabic allows several constructions with bāraka: blessing someone, in, upon, or for someone.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r12.anchor: وحكى الكسائي عن العرب: باركك الله، وبارك فيك. الثعلبي: العرب تقول باركك الله، وبارك فيك، وبارك عليك، وبارك لك، أربع لغات.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r13.speaker: شاعر مجهول
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r13.claim: A poem uses the blessing formula for birth, youth, and old age.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r13.anchor: قال الشاعر: فبوركت مولودا وبوركت ناشئا وبوركت عند الشيب إذ أنت أشيب

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r14.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r14.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the construction omits fī according to the idiom “God blessed you”; Moses was blessed at or near the fire, not inside it.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r14.anchor: الطبري: قال { بورك من في النار } ولم يقل بورك في من في النار على لغة من يقول باركك الله

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r15.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r15.claim: Al-Suddī says angels were in the fire and the blessing addressed Moses and the angels around it as an honorific greeting.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r15.anchor: وقال السدي: كان في النار ملائكة فالتبريك عائد إلى موسى والملائكة أي بورك فيك يا موسى وفي الملائكة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r16.claim: The greeting is compared to the angels’ greeting of Abraham’s household at 11:73.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r16.anchor: كما حيا إبراهيم على ألسنة الملائكة حين دخلوا عليه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r1.claim: They interpret the one in the fire as God Himself, understanding بورك as “be sanctified.”
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r1.anchor: قول ثالث قاله ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير: قدس من في النار وهو الله سبحانه وتعالى، عنى به نفسه تقدس وتعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومحمد بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r2.claim: They say the fire was God’s light: Moses saw a great light and mistook it for fire; God spoke and manifested signs from it without occupying a direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومحمد بن كعب: النار نور الله عز وجل نادى الله موسى وهو في النور وتأويل هذا أن موسى عليه السلام رأى نورا عظيما فظنه نارا

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r3.claim: God is not localized in heaven or earth; rather, His acts manifest everywhere and reveal the agent’s existence, as expressed at 43:84.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r3.anchor: لا أنه يتحيز فيهما، ولكن يظهر في كل فعل فيعلم به وجود الفاعل

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the blessing in the fire to mean God’s dominion and power.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r4.anchor: وقيل على هذا: أي بورك من في النار سلطانه وقدرته

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r5.claim: A further interpretation blesses what God placed in the fire as a sign.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: أي بورك ما في النار من أمر الله تعالى الذي جعله علامة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r6.speaker: أبو موسى
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r6.claim: A report from the Prophet says God neither sleeps nor should sleep, raises and lowers the scales, and is veiled by light; if uncovered, the radiance of His face would burn everything His sight reaches. Al-Qurṭubī cites Muslim and Ibn Mājah, with wording from Ibn Mājah.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r6.anchor: قلت: ومما يدل على صحة قول ابن عباس ما خرجه مسلم في «صحيحه»، وابن ماجه في «سننه» واللفظ له عن أبي موسى قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r7.speaker: أبو موسى
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r7.claim: Muslim’s fuller wording adds that night’s deeds are raised before day’s and day’s before night’s; another narration says the veil is fire. Al-Bayhaqī also transmits the report.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8#2/r7.anchor: ولفظ مسلم عن أبي موسى قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says the “radiances” are the majesty of God’s face; subḥān is glorification and declaring Him above imperfection.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: يقال السبحات إنها جلال وجهه، ومنها قيل: سبحان الله إنما هو تعظيم له وتنزيه

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r2.claim: The phrase may be an ellipsis for “those around it said, Glory be to God.”
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r2.anchor: والمعنى: أي ويقول من حولها { وسبحان الله } فحذف

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses spoke the glorification after hearing the call, seeking God’s aid and declaring Him transcendent.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن موسى عليه السلام قاله حين فرغ من سماع النداء استعانة بالله تعالى وتنزيها له قاله السدي

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r4.speaker: ابن شجرة
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r4.claim: Ibn Shajara says the phrase is God’s speech, blessing whoever glorifies the Lord of the worlds.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8-10/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول الله تعالى. ومعناه: وبورك فيمن سبح الله تعالى رب العالمين حكاه ابن شجرة
